rule_provenance.rule: When balancing multi-gene expression in E. coli synthetic pathways where inducer cost and expression noise must be minimized, apply a single promoter with 3'-UTR terminator bioparts of graded strength instead of multiple inducible promoters, because terminator control removes trans-acting-element-dependent initiation noise (≈4-fold lower intrinsic noise) while retaining tunable relative expression.

When tuning flux split between two consecutive products of a branched heterologous pathway in E. coli (validated for acetoin/2,3-BDO from pyruvate), apply an intercistronic Rho-independent terminator of chosen read-through strength to set downstream-enzyme expression, because the product ratio scales logarithmically with terminator read-through, allowing single-promoter, inducer-free pathway balancing.

When a heterologous production pathway in E. coli draws on glycolytic carbon and full knockout of the competing glycolytic step (pfkA) causes growth failure, apply a 3'-UTR terminator valve to reintroduce the blocked enzyme at graded expression levels in a ΔpfkA Δzwf background, because an intermediate glycolytic flux balances biomass generation against product flux; the optimal valve strength is host-dependent and must be screened per chassis (validated for myo-inositol production in MG1655 and genome-reduced eMS57 backgrounds).
